Emma — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the breakdown. Short answer: yes we can extend the POC and we have two practical ways to cover your workload without asking you to sign a year-long commit.

Options we typically propose for cases like yours:
- 10-day timebox extension + burst credit top-up: keep the existing POC terms, add a one-off burst credit pool (pre-bought tokens) that covers high-concurrency import windows. No long-term commit; one-time invoice.
- Short-term Sustained Seat bundle trial: provision 1–2 dedicated sustained seats on a 30-day trial rate (discounted) so daytime traffic gets consistent low-latency SLA; includes lower per-token cost but you pay for reserved capacity during the window.

Tradeoffs:
- MaxBurst add-on: lower commitment, good for spiky workloads, cheaper upfront for short tests, but if spikes become frequent it gets expensive.
- Sustained Seat bundle: higher predictable cost while reserved, better latency and tail guarantees — preferred if you expect consistent daytime QPS beyond the trial.

Suggested bridging offer (to avoid a heavy negotiation loop):
- 10 business day POC extension (no change to core contract)
- Add $6k of burst credits (covers ~150M tokens at your observed mix)
- If you convert to a 6-month paid trial within 45 days after the extended window, we’ll apply a $4k credit against the first invoice.

Cc’ing David to confirm the technical fit for the burst-credit sizing. Ben — looping you for pricing approval; we’ll keep this within standard uplift authority.

Best,

Emma / Ravi — reviewed the attachment and the usage sheet. A couple quick technical notes: 

- Burst credits map to additional reserved throughput windows on the same nodes; they don’t change model variants or tail-latency SLAs, but they do give you headroom for short import spikes.
- For the import pattern you shared (~10–12 minute spikes at ~8–10x baseline), the proposed $6k burst pool should be safe if imports remain <= 20/min avg and parallelism maxes at ~12. If you increase concurrency beyond that, costs scale linearly.
- If you want sustained low-99 latency across business hours, a single Sustained Seat reduces 99th percentile latency by ~30% in our benchmarks versus burst-only cases; the math favors seats once sustained load > ~40% of peak.

I recommend: take the short extension + burst credits to finish validation, but keep a low-friction path to test 1 sustained seat for 7–14 days before production flip. We can hot-add the seat mid-window if needed.

Happy to sync live tomorrow with Ravi if you want to walk through the import logs.

-David
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
